To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
active and passive networking are complementary in certain cases and substitute in others.

(i) passive networking complements active networking; (ii) active networking is more common among researchers who are not publishing bottlenecks; and (iii) the factors promoting participation in international conferences differ from those promoting European conference attendance.

(1) some types of passive networking complement active networking, while other types substitute for active networking, (2) geographic proximity to other researchers promotes networking, and (3) publishing bottlenecks are not a hindrance to networking.
